newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude near session lows late ahead of APIs.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude near session lows late ahead of APIs.

text.p: NYMEX crude hovered near its session lows late afternoon Tuesday, but the market was too timid to sharpen declines ahead of this evening's oil inventory data which could defy expectations, dealers said.

"Nobody wants to take big poistions either way in front of the APIs. Most are expecting a build in crude, and we have seen a build usually at this time, while a draw would be a real surprise," said Nauman Barakat, trader with Prudential Securities in New York.
At 1453 EST, April crude was off 33 cents a barrel at $20.16, near its session low of $20.10.
The April/May crude carry had widened to 16 cents from four cents Monday when prompt crude slipped into contango for the first time since May 1995.
Contango signifies the front month being the cheaper than the back month.
The American Petroleum Institute (API) is expected to report oil inventory data Tuesday evening for the week ended March 7.
Traders anticipate an increase in imports and relatively low crude runs to result in a build in crude stocks of around 3.5 million barrels.
Crude prices are sagging under an inlux of imports, particularly from West Africa, and low demand due to refinery maintenance.
Meanwhile, refined product losses trailed crude's.
April gasoline was off 0.51 cent a gallon at 63.85 cents, as the April crude-to-gasoline crack spread rose to $6.78 from $6.61 Monday.
The crack has risen more $1.50 in the past two weeks as dealers anticipate a seasonal rise in gasoline demand during the spring and summer.
April heating oil was off 0.23 cent a gallon at 52.85 cents, following losses in crude.
"There is very little volume," said a New York heating oil trader, explaining the lack of downside momentum in heat late session.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
